title: Clarity of Scripture
definition: The clarity of Scripture means that God's Word is given in such a way that its central message of salvation, faith, obedience, and godly living can be understood by ordinary people who read it humbly.
summary: Not every passage is equally simple, but God speaks clearly enough to call sinners to Christ and guide His people in truth.
christFocus: The clarity of Scripture shines in its witness to Christ, the Gospel, repentance, faith, and discipleship.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Clarity of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to clarity of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
